title: Algorithmic Non-commutative Class Field Theory: Hecke operators, sandpile groups and operator algebras on trees and buildings, with applications
description:
Volume I of a two-volume work: a monograph of 26 chapters assembled from twenty papers (September 2026) and four applied notes, with the verification scripts, data tables and figures that reproduce every numerical claim. Volume II, Algebraic Genomics, is published separately.

For a finite (q+1)-regular graph — an arithmetic quotient of the Bruhat–Tits tree of PGL2 — the sandpile (critical) group of the Hecke–Laplacian has order a product of inverse local L-values, so Frobenius traces appear as K-theoretic torsion. The book develops what this group does along towers of graphs (exact Iwasawa control for abelian voltage towers, a second-order exceptional zero with a rational L-invariant that no odd cyclic class computes, and a non-commutative degeneracy calculus with λ = −1 for the Iwahori tower), which operator algebras carry it (a trace obstruction forbids Cuntz–Krieger realizations of the Ihara companion; shadow graphs realize Z ⊕ Jac(Y) as K0 of Kirchberg algebras whose inductive limit has torsion K0 dual to the sandpile pro-module; the kernel of the tail norm is the q-torsion for every q; the head map gives a C*-correspondence with K0-index the head pushforward), and what changes in higher rank (Ã2 and Ãd buildings: no trace obstruction, no abelian towers, and an unconditional unitarity theorem placing the parahoric zeros of the edge zeta on the critical circle in every rank, on an invariant subspace produced by one flag count in PG(d,q)). Part V applies the machinery outside number theory: Bloch effective mass on tree lattices, what the boundary algebra of p-adic AdS/CFT cannot see, an algebraic normality certificate for graph towers, and power-sum bounds for hidden eigenvalues of positive realizations.

Every result is labelled proved, quoted, computationally verified or conjectural; the closing chapter lists what is solved, open and impossible. Text: CC BY 4.0. Code: MIT.
